meta.sourceDocument: Tutolingo demo pack (mock data for testing)
meta.learnerProfile: Mock learner: Lucía, 22, student, likes travel, music and football. Preparing for a trip to Ireland.
meta.theme: Everyday English for travel and social life
meta.notes: MOCK DATA — switch it off in Profile → Demo content to go back to your own content/tutolingo-content.json.

vocabulary.definition: the bags and suitcases you take when you travel

example.target: Lucía put her luggage in the overhead rack.
example.native: Lucía puso su equipaje en el portaequipajes.

vocabulary.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another

example.target: The journey to Galway takes three hours.
example.native: El viaje a Galway tarda tres horas.

vocabulary.definition: a situation in which something happens later than planned

example.target: There was a delay of forty minutes.
example.native: Hubo un retraso de cuarenta minutos.

vocabulary.definition: full of people

example.target: The bus was crowded in the morning.
example.native: El autobús estaba lleno de gente por la mañana.

vocabulary.definition: a line of people waiting for something

example.target: We waited in a long queue for tickets.
example.native: Esperamos en una cola larga para las entradas.

vocabulary.definition: a piece of paper that shows you have paid

example.target: Keep the receipt in case you need a refund.
example.native: Guarda el recibo por si necesitas un reembolso.

vocabulary.definition: money returned to you when you are not happy with something

example.target: Lucía asked for a refund for the cancelled tour.
example.native: Lucía pidió un reembolso por el tour cancelado.

vocabulary.definition: visiting interesting places as a tourist

example.target: We went sightseeing around the old town.
example.native: Hicimos turismo por el casco antiguo.

vocabulary.definition: a famous building or place that is easy to recognise

example.target: The bridge is the city's most photographed landmark.
example.native: El puente es el monumento más fotografiado de la ciudad.

vocabulary.definition: to pay to use something for a short time

example.target: They hired bikes for the weekend.
example.native: Alquilaron bicicletas para el fin de semana.

vocabulary.definition: an arrangement you make in advance

example.target: I have a booking for two nights.
example.native: Tengo una reserva para dos noches.

vocabulary.definition: a case with a handle used for carrying clothes when travelling

example.target: Her suitcase was too heavy to carry upstairs.
example.native: Su maleta era demasiado pesada para subirla.

vocabulary.definition: very happy and interested about something that is going to happen

example.target: Lucía is excited about her first trip abroad.
example.native: Lucía está emocionada por su primer viaje al extranjero.

vocabulary.definition: unhappy because you are thinking about problems

example.target: She was worried about missing the train.
example.native: Estaba preocupada por perder el tren.

vocabulary.definition: showing good manners towards other people

example.target: It is polite to say thank you.
example.native: Es educado dar las gracias.

vocabulary.definition: to take something from someone and give it back later

example.target: Can I borrow your charger for an hour?
example.native: ¿Puedo pedirte prestado tu cargador una hora?

vocabulary.definition: to ask someone to come to an event

example.target: They invited me to a birthday party.
example.native: Me invitaron a una fiesta de cumpleaños.

vocabulary.definition: to talk in a friendly and informal way

example.target: We chatted about music for an hour.
example.native: Charlamos sobre música durante una hora.

vocabulary.definition: to tell someone that something is good and worth trying

example.target: Can you recommend a good coffee shop?
example.native: ¿Puedes recomendarme una buena cafetería?

vocabulary.definition: pleasant to wear, sit in or use

example.target: These shoes are comfortable for walking.
example.native: Estos zapatos son cómodos para caminar.

vocabulary.definition: able to be used or obtained

example.target: Are there any tickets available for Friday?
example.native: ¿Hay entradas disponibles para el viernes?

vocabulary.definition: a plan of times for activities

example.target: The train schedule changes at weekends.
example.native: El horario de trenes cambia los fines de semana.

vocabulary.definition: to get pleasure from something

example.target: I really enjoyed the live music.
example.native: Disfruté mucho de la música en directo.

vocabulary.definition: to have enough money for something

example.target: We can't afford a hotel in the centre.
example.native: No podemos permitirnos un hotel en el centro.

grammar.title: Present Simple
grammar.rule: Use the present simple for routines, habits and facts. Add -s or -es with he, she and it.
grammar.nativeRule: Usamos el presente simple para rutinas y hechos. Con he, she, it el verbo lleva -s o -es.

examples.native: El tren sale a las ocho.

examples.target: The hostel costs thirty euros a night.
examples.native: El albergue cuesta treinta euros la noche.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the -s: «She study» instead of «She studies».

exercises.prompt: The museum ___ at nine o'clock.
They ___ to the coast every summer.
exercises.explanation: Plural subject keeps the base form.

exercises.prompt: She ___ three languages.
It ___ a lot in November here.
exercises.explanation: A general fact about the weather.

grammar.title: Present Continuous
grammar.rule: Use am / is / are + verb-ing for actions happening now or around now.
grammar.nativeRule: Usamos am / is / are + verbo-ing para acciones que pasan ahora.

examples.target: We are waiting for the bus.
She is studying for an exam this week.
examples.native: Esta semana estudia para un examen.

examples.target: They are travelling to Dublin on Friday.

commonMistakes: Mixing it with the present simple: «I am go» instead of «I am going».

exercises.prompt: Look! The bus ___.
I ___ for my exam this week.
They ___ dinner at the moment.
Why ___ you laughing?

grammar.title: Past Simple
grammar.rule: Use the past simple for finished actions. Regular verbs add -ed; irregular verbs have their own form.
grammar.nativeRule: Usamos el pasado simple para acciones terminadas. Los verbos regulares añaden -ed.

examples.target: Lucía booked the hostel last month.
examples.native: Lucía reservó el albergue el mes pasado.

exercises.prompt: We ___ the old town last Sunday.
She ___ her ticket at the gate.
They ___ to Galway by coach.
___ you enjoy the concert?
exercises.explanation: Questions in the past use did.

grammar.title: Comparatives & Superlatives
grammar.rule: Short adjectives take -er / -est; longer adjectives take more / most. Irregular: good → better → best.
grammar.nativeRule: Adjetivos cortos: -er / -est. Largos: more / most. Irregulares: good → better → best.
grammar.structure: adj-er than / the adj-est · more + adj than / the most + adj

examples.target: The bus is cheaper than the train.
examples.native: El autobús es más barato que el tren.

examples.target: That was the best coffee in town.
examples.native: Ese fue el mejor café de la ciudad.
Galway es más pequeño que Dublín.

exercises.prompt: The bus is ___ than the train.
This is the ___ hotel in the city.
The centre is ___ than the suburbs.
January is the ___ month of the year here.

grammar.title: First Conditional
grammar.rule: If + present simple, will + base verb. Use it for real possibilities in the future.
grammar.nativeRule: If + presente simple, will + verbo base. Para posibilidades reales en el futuro.
grammar.structure: If + present simple, will + base verb

examples.target: If it rains, we will stay inside.
If you book online, you will save money.
If the weather is good, we will walk to the cliffs.
examples.native: Si hace buen tiempo, caminaremos hasta los acantilados.

exercises.prompt: If it ___, we will stay inside.
exercises.explanation: After if we use the present simple.

exercises.prompt: If you book online, you ___ money.
She ___ happy if you call her.
exercises.explanation: Will + base verb in the result.

exercises.prompt: If we leave now, we ___ the train.

grammar.title: Prepositions of Time
grammar.rule: Use in for months, years and parts of the day; on for days and dates; at for clock times.
grammar.nativeRule: In para meses/años, on para días, at para horas.
grammar.structure: at + time · on + day/date · in + month/year

examples.native: El tour empieza a las diez.
Llegamos el viernes por la mañana.

examples.target: The museum is closed in January.
examples.native: El museo está cerrado en enero.

exercises.prompt: The tour starts ___ ten o'clock.
We arrived ___ Friday.
Ireland is beautiful ___ spring.
The festival is ___ July.

idioms.meaning: to make people feel relaxed when they first meet

example.target: He told a joke to break the ice at the hostel.
example.native: Contó un chiste para romper el hielo en el hostal.

idioms.usageNotes: Very common in social and classroom situations.

idioms.meaning: to learn how to do something with practice

example.target: The metro app was confusing, but I got the hang of it.
example.native: La app del metro era confusa, pero le cogí el truco.

example.target: I'm a bit under the weather today, so I'll rest.
example.native: Hoy estoy un poco pachucha, así que descansaré.

example.target: Let's hit the road before the traffic gets bad.
example.native: Pongámonos en camino antes de que haya tráfico.

example.target: The online check-in was a piece of cake.
example.native: El check-in online fue pan comido.

idioms.meaning: to watch and take care of something

example.target: Could you keep an eye on my luggage?
example.native: ¿Podrías echar un ojo a mi equipaje?

idioms.meaning: to feel happy and excited about something in the future

example.target: I'm looking forward to the weekend trip.
example.native: Tengo ganas de la excursión del fin de semana.

idioms.usageNotes: Followed by a noun or verb-ing.

idioms.meaning: to use all of something so there is none left

example.target: We ran out of cash on the last day.
example.native: Nos quedamos sin efectivo el último día.

example.target: Take your time — the train isn't until six.
example.native: Tómate tu tiempo, el tren no sale hasta las seis.

example.target: Let's make sure we're on the same page about the plan.
example.native: Asegurémonos de estar en la misma sintonía con el plan.

conversations.title: At the train station
conversations.setting: Buying a ticket at the counter
conversations.goal: Buy a ticket and ask about times
conversations.nativeSummary: Comprar un billete y preguntar por los horarios.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Hello, I'd like a ticket to Galway, please.
turns.native: Hola, querría un billete a Galway, por favor.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Clerk
turns.target: Single or return?
turns.native: ¿Solo ida o ida y vuelta?

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Return, coming back on Sunday.
turns.native: Ida y vuelta, volviendo el domingo.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Clerk
turns.target: That's thirty-two euros. The next train leaves at ten past nine.
turns.native: Son treinta y dos euros. El próximo tren sale a las nueve y diez.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Is there a delay today?
turns.native: ¿Hay retraso hoy?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Clerk
turns.target: No, everything is on time. Platform four.
turns.native: No, todo va puntual. Andén cuatro.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Great, could I have a receipt?
turns.native: Genial, ¿me da un recibo?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Clerk
turns.target: Of course. Have a good journey!
turns.native: Por supuesto. ¡Buen viaje!

conversations.title: Checking into the hostel
conversations.nativeSummary: Registrarse en el hostel y preguntar por los servicios.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Hi, I have a booking for two nights.
turns.native: Hola, tengo una reserva para dos noches.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Receptionist
turns.target: Welcome! Can I see your passport, please?
turns.native: ¡Bienvenida! ¿Puedo ver su pasaporte, por favor?

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Here you are. What time is breakfast?
turns.native: Aquí tiene. ¿A qué hora es el desayuno?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Receptionist
turns.target: From seven to ten in the kitchen downstairs.
turns.native: De siete a diez en la cocina de abajo.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Is there anywhere to leave my luggage after check-out?
turns.native: ¿Hay algún sitio para dejar el equipaje después del check-out?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Receptionist
turns.target: Yes, the storage room is free until six.
turns.native: Sí, la sala de equipajes es gratis hasta las seis.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Perfect. Could you recommend a good place for dinner?
turns.native: Perfecto. ¿Podría recomendarme un buen sitio para cenar?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Receptionist
turns.target: The fish place on the corner is excellent.
turns.native: El sitio de pescado de la esquina es excelente.

keyPhrases.target: I have a booking for two nights.
keyPhrases.native: Tengo una reserva para dos noches.

keyPhrases.target: Could you recommend a good place for dinner?
keyPhrases.native: ¿Podría recomendarme un buen sitio para cenar?

conversations.title: Small talk about the weekend
conversations.goal: Talk about plans and react naturally
conversations.nativeSummary: Charlar sobre los planes del fin de semana.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Any plans for the weekend?
turns.native: ¿Algún plan para el fin de semana?

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Mark
turns.target: I'm going hiking on Saturday if the weather is good.
turns.native: Voy a hacer senderismo el sábado si hace buen tiempo.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Nice! I've never been hiking.
turns.native: ¡Qué bien! Nunca he hecho senderismo.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Mark
turns.target: You should come. It's not hard — you'll get the hang of it.
turns.native: Deberías venir. No es difícil, le cogerás el truco.

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Sounds fun, but I'm a bit under the weather.
turns.native: Suena divertido, pero estoy un poco pachucha.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Mark
turns.target: Then take your time and rest. Maybe next weekend?
turns.native: Entonces tómate tu tiempo y descansa. ¿Quizá el próximo?

turns.speaker: A
turns.name: Lucía
turns.target: Yes, I'd look forward to that.
turns.native: Sí, me encantaría.

turns.speaker: B
turns.name: Mark
turns.target: Great, I'll text you the details.
turns.native: Genial, te mando los detalles por mensaje.

keyPhrases.native: ¿Algún plan para el fin de semana?
Te mando los detalles por mensaje.
